chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both), that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"There is no harm in hunting birds if they have seized [caught] both their wings." The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And if one finds an egg and does not know whether it is from what is permissible to eat or from what is forbidden to eat, let him examine it; if it is equal [symmetrical] at both ends, he should avoid it, and if it is different [asymmetrical] at the ends, he may eat it. (57) 57 Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from Fudalah, from Al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) who said: 'When you enter a thicket and find an egg, do not eat it except that which differs at its ends.'"
ai.seo_question: What is the method for determining if a wild egg is halal or haram to eat according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical jurisprudence of hunting, emphasizing the physical state of the prey (captured by wings) as a condition for validity. It further introduces a distinctive heuristic for distinguishing permissible from impermissible wild eggs based on morphological symmetry, reflecting the Shia scholarly approach to deriving rulings from observable natural signs when explicit textual evidence is absent.
